summary: recce/services/etcd.py implements a shallow reachability probe: /version + /health fingerprint, GET /v2/keys/?recursive=true, and POST /v3/kv/range with the full-range 0x00..0x00 key. It counts keys but never extracts or classifies them, never touches maintenance/auth/cluster/debug endpoints, never probes the peer port, and never tests write. Findings are two-state (unauth-read vs auth-protected) — the module leaves the highest-value etcd primitives (snapshot download, member list, default-cred auth, k8s Secret harvesting, pprof heap) unrealized, and produces no cross-service artifacts (SA tokens, peer URLs, TLS SANs) that a kube-apiserver or scanner module could consume.
existing_capabilities: HTTP with automatic TLS fallback via _http()
v2 unauth read via GET /v2/keys/?recursive=true with recursive node count
v3 unauth read via POST /v3/kv/range with base64(0x00) range span
Two findings: critical etcd_unauth_read + info etcd_authed
svcprobe integration with budget/progress; findings_to_vulns wire-up

missing_capabilities.name: Snapshot download (POST /v3/maintenance/snapshot)
missing_capabilities.description: etcd v3 exposes a streaming full-DB dump via /v3/maintenance/snapshot returning the entire bbolt file (all keys, revisions, tombstones — including deleted Secrets recoverable from historical revisions). Frequently unauth on the same permission tier as /v3/kv/range but also independently reachable on some misconfigurations where kv/range is filtered. This is THE etcd crown-jewel primitive and the module never touches it. Recovered file also feeds offline bbolt walking to defeat compaction.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: etcd API v3 maintenance.proto Snapshot RPC / Documentation/dev-guide/api_reference_v3.md#service-maintenance

missing_capabilities.name: Kubernetes payload extraction from kvs
missing_capabilities.description: When /v3/kv/range succeeds, the module counts kvs and discards them. The keys/values are protobuf-serialized k8s objects at well-known prefixes (/registry/secrets/<ns>/<name>, /registry/serviceaccounts/, /registry/configmaps/, /registry/apiextensions.k8s.io/, /registry/certificatesigningrequests/). Parsing the Secret ObjectMeta+Data recovers cleartext ServiceAccount JWTs, kubelet client cert PEMs, kubeconfig blobs, image-pull secrets, and TLS keys — every credential in the cluster. Currently zero of this is emitted.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: kubernetes/pkg/registry/core/secret + apimachinery protobuf wire format; etcd Documentation/op-guide/recovery.md

missing_capabilities.name: Default-credential authentication (POST /v3/auth/authenticate)
missing_capabilities.description: When --auth is enabled, module returns info-only. It should attempt /v3/auth/authenticate with the seeded pairs root/root, root/'', root/etcd, root/password, root/admin (v3.0 defaults; also 'guest' role). A successful auth returns a bearer token usable via 'Authorization: <token>' against every other endpoint — bypasses the auth-protected verdict entirely. Also try /v2/auth for legacy pre-3.2 clusters.

missing_capabilities.name: Member/peer enumeration (POST /v3/cluster/member/list)
missing_capabilities.description: MemberList RPC returns every member's peerURLs, clientURLs, name, and 64-bit member ID. Frequently unauth-readable when kv/range is denied (auth check applies per-tier). Reveals internal DNS names (etcd-0.etcd.kube-system.svc), private IPs of the entire control plane, and hostnames of the apiserver certs. Cross-service intel: those hostnames belong in the host discovery pool for other service modules (kubernetes.py, http.py).

missing_capabilities.name: Peer/gRPC-raft port (2380) never probed
missing_capabilities.description: is_etcd() matches 2380 but probe() only ever hits the client port. The peer port speaks the raft protocol; when --peer-client-cert-auth is off (independent flag from --client-cert-auth), an attacker can add a rogue member via MemberAdd against the client API's cluster endpoint on the peer port, then raft-replicate arbitrary state — this is a full-cluster compromise even against v3-auth-enabled clusters. At minimum GET /raft/status and GET /v2/stats/self should be tried on 2380.

missing_capabilities.name: Debug/pprof endpoints (/debug/pprof/*, /debug/vars)
missing_capabilities.description: etcd bakes in net/http/pprof at /debug/pprof/{heap,goroutine,profile,cmdline,trace}. /debug/pprof/heap dumps process memory (containing decrypted secrets, gRPC creds, bearer tokens in flight); /debug/pprof/cmdline reveals the full argv (--cert-file, --peer-key-file paths, ETCDCTL_API=3 env). /debug/vars leaks module-level state. All are typically bound to the same listener as /metrics with no auth.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Go net/http/pprof; etcd main.go enablePprof; CVE-2019-11248 (same class in kubelet)

missing_capabilities.name: Prometheus /metrics endpoint
missing_capabilities.description: GET /metrics returns Prometheus text: etcd_server_id, etcd_cluster_version, etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total, etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds, grpc_server_started_total{grpc_method=...}. Discloses leader ID, DB size (hint at how many secrets exist), version at fine granularity for CVE mapping, and which RPCs are being served. Almost always unauth (separate --listen-metrics-urls flag, default no auth).

missing_capabilities.name: Write-capability probe (canary PUT)
missing_capabilities.description: Module only tests read. A POST /v3/kv/put with key=base64('/recce-probe-canary') value=base64(random) followed by immediate delete determines whether the anonymous role has write, which is a categorically worse finding: an attacker can write ValidatingWebhookConfiguration entries, forge RBAC ClusterRoleBindings, plant a mutating admission webhook, or insert a ServiceAccount token — full k8s takeover without touching the apiserver.

missing_capabilities.name: v2 stats endpoints (/v2/stats/self, /v2/stats/leader, /v2/stats/store)
missing_capabilities.description: Even on v3-only clusters the v2 stats subtree is usually left mounted. /v2/stats/self returns name, id, state (leader/follower), leaderInfo.leader, startTime. /v2/stats/leader returns follower ID map with RTT and fail counts. /v2/stats/store returns setSuccess/setFail/getsSuccess counters — usable to fingerprint compaction and activity. Cheap unauth intel the module ignores.

missing_capabilities.name: Auth introspection (user/list, role/list, status)
missing_capabilities.description: POST /v3/auth/status returns enabled bool + auth revision without a token; /v3/auth/user/list and /v3/auth/role/list often need only root but leak on misconfig. Even the enabled bit from /v3/auth/status differentiates 'auth off' from 'auth on but readable' — the current module can only infer this from a 200 vs 401 on kv/range, missing the case where kv/range returns empty because of RBAC scoping (looks unreadable but read-with-creds would work).

missing_capabilities.name: Lease enumeration (POST /v3/lease/leases)
missing_capabilities.description: LeaseLeases lists every active lease ID with TTL. In a k8s cluster each control-plane lease is a holder identity — kube-controller-manager/leader, kube-scheduler/leader, node-lease/<nodeName> — reading one lease's associated keys gives you the current leader hostname and every registered kubelet identity. Also feeds pivot targeting.

missing_capabilities.name: TLS certificate CN/SAN extraction
missing_capabilities.description: When _http() falls through to HTTPS the server cert is available via getpeercert() but discarded. etcd server certs typically SAN etcd internal DNS (etcd-0.etcd, controlplane-1.internal), the CN of the CA (kubernetes, kubernetes-front-proxy), and sometimes apiserver hostnames. These are host-discovery gold that no scanner input feeds today.

missing_capabilities.name: Version-to-CVE mapping
missing_capabilities.description: version is captured but never mapped to known CVEs: CVE-2020-15106 (gateway crash), CVE-2020-15112 (integer overflow in decoding), CVE-2020-15113 (--data-dir directory traversal), CVE-2020-15114 (gateway TLS bypass), CVE-2021-28235 (auth token deserialization on 3.4.10-), CVE-2023-32082 (auth bypass with basic auth + password change race). Version string is already parsed; ranged comparison would produce a distinct severity finding per applicable CVE without adding new traffic.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MITRE CVE entries above; etcd security advisories at github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories

missing_capabilities.name: Maintenance status/alarm/hashKV (POST /v3/maintenance/{status,alarm,hash})
missing_capabilities.description: Status returns raftIndex, raftTerm, leader member ID, dbSize, dbSizeInUse, isLearner. Hash returns full-store hash. Alarm returns cluster health alarms (NOSPACE, CORRUPT). All feed the same cluster-intel picture and are separately gated from kv/range on many deployments. dbSize is a direct predictor of secret volume for triaging targets.

missing_capabilities.name: gRPC-native path via HTTP/2 h2c
missing_capabilities.description: Module uses http.client which is HTTP/1.1 only, so it interacts with the gRPC-JSON gateway. Real gRPC (POST with Content-Type: application/grpc, h2c or TLS-ALPN) sometimes has different auth handling and reveals streaming RPCs (Watch, LeaseKeepAlive) that the gateway doesn't fully proxy. Marginal for a scanner but a real gap in fidelity.

priority_gaps: 1. Snapshot download via POST /v3/maintenance/snapshot — full bbolt dump including historical (uncompacted) revisions of deleted Secrets; the single highest-value etcd primitive currently absent.

2. K8s Secret / ServiceAccount decoding from kvs — the module already retrieves the values on unauth read but throws them away instead of protobuf-decoding /registry/secrets/ and /registry/serviceaccounts/ into bearer tokens for the credential broker.
3. Default-credential authenticate against /v3/auth/authenticate (root/root, root/'', root/etcd) — turns every 'etcd_authed' info finding into a potential critical.
4. Cluster/MemberList via POST /v3/cluster/member/list — internal peer URLs, IPs, DNS names; cross-service host discovery input.
5. Peer port 2380 probing — is_etcd() already matches it but probe() never contacts it; --peer-client-cert-auth is a separately configured flag frequently left off and permits raft MemberAdd.
6. Write-capability probe (canary PUT) — distinguishes unauth-read from unauth-write, the latter is full-cluster RCE.
7. /debug/pprof/heap and /debug/pprof/cmdline — process-memory dump and argv leak with cert/key paths.
8. /metrics — leader ID, dbSize, cluster_version, per-RPC counters, unauth by default (--listen-metrics-urls).
9. /v2/stats/{self,leader,store} — leader disclosure and follower topology on nearly every install.
10. Version-to-CVE mapping — CVE-2020-15113/15114, CVE-2021-28235, CVE-2023-32082; version already captured, no extra traffic.
cross_service_wire_gaps: ServiceAccount JWTs and kubelet client certs recovered from /registry/secrets/ are not emitted as creds — a kubernetes.py / kube-apiserver module would use them for authenticated attacks but nothing hands them over.

Peer/clientURLs returned by /v3/cluster/member/list are internal hostnames/IPs that should feed the host-discovery input for other service modules (kubernetes.py, http.py, docker.py, docker_registry.py) but are not surfaced.
TLS server-cert SANs seen during the HTTPS fallback are discarded rather than added as host aliases; kube-apiserver certs frequently share the etcd CA.
A successful default-cred authenticate would yield an etcd bearer token; there is no cred store to publish it to for other collaborators — the finding would be one-shot.
dbSize from /v3/maintenance/status is a natural signal for cluster-severity ranking in the aggregate report but is not produced.

Leader member ID and follower peer IDs (from /v2/stats/leader and /v3/maintenance/status) would let the reporting layer group multi-host etcd findings under one logical cluster; today each host is an island.
notes: Tests confirm coverage matches the module: v3 kvs read, v2 nodes read, auth-401 fallback, dead port. No test exercises snapshot, member list, auth, pprof, metrics, peer port, or TLS SAN — because the module never calls them. `_finding()` builds a single finding shape (svccommon-compatible) so adding new kinds is cheap. `analyze()` already routes through svcprobe with budget/progress so additional probe calls just need to be added inside `probe()` and surfaced in the returned dict.
